desc:
Shopify inventory control and stock alerts give you stock numbers you can trust, so customers never buy what you cannot ship. Ecom Swift LLC checks your counts, corrects mismatches, sets low-stock alerts and writes a simple routine for supplier updates.

## What is Shopify inventory control?

Shopify inventory control is the practice of keeping the quantity shown in your store equal to the quantity you really have. It covers the counts for each variant, the thresholds that warn you when stock runs low, and the rules for what happens when an item sells out.

Shopify tracks stock for you, but only as well as the numbers you enter. When counts drift away from the shelf or the supplier file, the store starts making promises you cannot keep.

## Why wrong stock numbers hurt a store

Overselling is the most visible problem. A customer pays for an item, and then you must write to say it is not available. That means a refund, a lost sale and a customer who may not return. Underselling is quieter but just as costly: an item that is in stock but shows as sold out sends shoppers elsewhere.

Wrong numbers also waste your time. You spend hours checking sheets and supplier emails, and you reorder too late or too much. Dead stock ties up cash, while best sellers run dry at the worst moment.

## How accurate stock supports sales and trust

Accurate stock makes every other part of the store work better. Product pages can show honest availability, so shoppers trust what they see. Collections can hide or label sold-out items, which keeps the page full of things people can buy. Your ads and emails send traffic to products that are really available.

Alerts add timing. A low-stock warning arrives while you still have time to reorder, instead of after customers have already hit an empty page. Over time, a stable routine means less firefighting and more attention for the things that grow the business.

## What good inventory control includes

- A count check of your variants against your own sheet or supplier file.
- Corrections made directly in Shopify, with the old values recorded.
- A low-stock threshold for each product, written down and applied.
- Email alerts that reach the right person when stock falls to that level.
- A clear sold-out setting for each product: hide, label or allow back-orders.
- Back-in-stock handling so returning items reach customers again.
- A supplier update routine that says who updates what, and when.
- Location setup if you hold stock in more than one place.
- A reusable spreadsheet for bulk quantity updates.
- An inventory export before and after, so you can see what changed.

## What we do

We export your current inventory from Shopify and compare it with the source you trust, whether that is your own sheet or a supplier file. Every mismatch is listed, and we correct them in the admin once you confirm which number is right.

Next we set thresholds and turn on alerts, and we decide with you how sold-out products should behave on the storefront. On the Standard package we write the supplier update routine in plain steps that anyone on your team can follow. Premium covers larger catalogs, up to three locations, a bulk update sheet you can reuse and a reorder level list by product. We do not count your physical stock, so the shelf count is yours to provide.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Choose one place as the source of truth for stock.
- Update Shopify the same day that stock arrives or leaves.
- Set low-stock levels based on how long your supplier takes to deliver.
- Review sold-out products every week.
- Keep one clean export as a record of a known good state.

**Avoid:**
- Selling the same stock on several channels without a shared count.
- Setting every threshold to the same number regardless of the product.
- Leaving sold-out products live with no label or alternative.
- Editing quantities in several places at once.
- Ignoring variants such as size and color, which carry separate counts.

## Who this is for

This service suits sellers who have oversold at least once and want it to stop. It also suits dropshippers whose supplier files change often, and shops with more than one location, a pop-up stand or a warehouse. If you are about to run a big sale, a count check beforehand protects the campaign.

## What we need from you

Send a collaborator or staff invitation, and your own stock sheet or supplier file in any common format. Tell us how long reorders take and who should receive the alerts. We never need your password. Automatic syncing with a supplier depends on what your supplier provides, so we describe the routine that fits your situation. After you order, we confirm the plan and the files we need before we start.
